extracted.intended_audience: NLP/AI researchers and practitioners developing or evaluating LLM creative-writing capabilities
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and applying automated evaluation methods to judge the creativity of texts generated by large language models, using reference-based, product-focused metrics inspired by the Torrance Test of Creative Writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW) as the foundational framework for evaluating creativity, treating creativity as a product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper adopts TTCW to ground automated evaluation; while the abstract does not enumerate TTCW subdimensions, TTCW is presented as the theoretical basis for product-based creativity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate creativity as product
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the creativity of generated texts by evaluating the produced artifact (the text) rather than the creative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed method explicitly frames creativity-as-product, i.e., scoring outputs themselves against criteria/references rather than attempting to model internal generation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-based Likert-style scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Score generated creative texts using Likert-style ratings relative to high-quality reference texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method compares model outputs to curated high-quality reference examples and assigns Likert-scale scores, enabling comparative judgments across multiple tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score relative to high-quality reference texts across tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple test items and score model outputs in relation to exemplar reference texts across those tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approach is explicitly reference-based and applied across various test items to provide robust, comparative evaluation; the abstract emphasizes scoring 'relative to high-quality reference texts across various tests.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with human assessments (pairwise accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how well automated evaluations agree with human judgments, e.g., via pairwise accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment with human assessments is a core objective; the paper reports improved alignment (pairwise accuracy = 0.75, +15%) as evidence of method effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce reliance on costly manual annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an automated evaluation alternative that avoids or reduces expensive human annotation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation stated in the abstract: existing methods often rely on costly manual annotations or poorly match human judgments; the proposed reference-based method is presented as a cost-effective solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to LLM-generated creative writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation method should be applicable to creative-writing outputs produced by large language models (stories, literature, storytelling tasks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper focuses on LLMs' creative-writing capability and targets evaluation across creative domains such as literature and storytelling.
